text:
Our Nights stick has 250 mg of magnesium. That number means different things on different labels, so here is how to read it.

Many labels show the weight of the whole compound, not the magnesium inside it. Magnesium bisglycinate is only about 14% magnesium by weight, so a 1,000 mg tablet can hold around 140 mg of actual magnesium. When you compare products, look for the elemental figure.

We use bisglycinate because it is generally gentle on the stomach, and we print the dose on the pack.

What do the studies say? A four-week, placebo-controlled trial in adults with poor sleep gave 250 mg of elemental magnesium as bisglycinate and reported a modest improvement in insomnia severity. Sleep was self-reported, and the authors asked for longer studies with objective measures. A recent review of 12 trials was more cautious still. The evidence looks strongest for people who are low in magnesium and weaker for everyone else.

That is why magnesium is one of four ingredients in Nights and not the whole story. Each ingredient has a lab report on our site that you can read next to its dose.

When you compare a magnesium product, what do you look at first: the elemental dose, the form, or the lab report?
